newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban seize heroin from air passengers.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban seize heroin from air passengers.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamist Taleban militia said it had seized 14 kg (30 pounds) of heroin from Delhi-bound passengers at Jalalabad airport on Friday.

It was the first major drug seizure announced by the Taleban since its forces captured the eastern city of Jalalabad on September 11. The radical Islamic movement has recently appeared to harden its attitude towards the thriving Afghan narcotics trade.

Mullah Alladad, the Taleban commander in control of the airport in the eastern city, told Reuters by telephone that the drugs had been found in the bags of four Afghans about to board a flight to Delhi on state-run Ariana Airline.
"They have been handed over to the concerned authorities for further interrogation," he said.
Alladad quoted one of the alleged drug couriers as saying during preliminary questioning that the heroin had been brought from Pakistan's tribal area bordering Afghanistan.
Last month the Taleban was reported to have announced a complete ban on opium poppy cultivation.
Iran has accused the Taleban of encouraging the drugs trade in western Afghanistan on the Iranian border, a charge the Taleban deny.
Drug enforcement officials say India is one transit route for heroin destined for Europe and North America.
